question: What is the primary role of computers in modern nursing informatics?

options.B: Managing patient records and health data

explanation: Computers in informatics primarily support the storage, retrieval, and management of health data to improve patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why is it important for a clinical nurse to understand computer classifications?

options.A: It replaces the need for standard pharmacology knowledge
options.B: It is required to write complex medical software algorithms
options.C: It assists in operating hospital digital infrastructure effectively
options.D: It enables nurses to repair broken computer motherboards

explanation: Knowing device capabilities helps clinicians use hospital hardware correctly for electronic records and patient monitoring. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which computer type processes information using discrete binary digits?
explanation: Digital computers operate on discrete data represented as binary code, which is standard for modern hospital software. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h2)

question: An intensive care unit monitor that measures continuous physical patient signals and converts them into numerical data is an example of what computer type?
explanation: Hybrid systems merge continuous analog data collection with digital processing, making them ideal for complex critical care monitors. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h2)

question: What primary factors determine the traditional classification of computers by size and power?

options.A: Keyboard layout and mouse connection type
options.B: Screen color, brand name, and manufacturing country
options.C: Physical dimensions, memory capacity, and processing speed
options.D: Power outlet voltage and external plastic casing color

explanation: Computers are traditionally grouped by their physical footprint, memory size, and overall computational strength. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is a major consequence of technological advancements in computer hardware sizing?

options.A: Hardware becomes entirely obsolete across all industries
options.B: Processing power increases while physical size decreases
options.C: Computers become larger as their memory capacity shrinks
options.D: Processing speed slows down to accommodate smaller chips

explanation: Modern engineering allows smaller devices to deliver immense processing capabilities previously restricted to room-sized machines. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which of the following is a common healthcare application of microcomputers?

options.C: Managing the entire global meteorological network

explanation: Microcomputers like tablets and desktop terminals are standard tools used directly by nurses for patient charting and medication scans. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h4)

question: What defines the core architecture of a microcomputer?

options.A: Requiring an entire dedicated air-conditioned room to operate
options.B: Processing data exclusively through magnetic tape storage
options.C: A central processing unit housed on a single integrated chip
options.D: Using purely analog signals to measure patient pressure

explanation: The defining feature of a microcomputer is its microprocessor, which places the central processing unit onto a single silicon chip. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is a primary function of a mainframe computer in a large hospital?

options.A: Providing a personal workstation for an individual clinic nurse
options.B: Measuring continuous analog blood pressure waveforms at the bedside
options.C: Managing enterprise-wide electronic health records and databases
options.D: Serving as a portable handheld device for single-patient charting

explanation: Mainframes possess the immense capacity required to run centralized, hospital-wide record systems and large databases safely. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h5)

question: What key operational advantage do mainframe computers offer healthcare institutions?

options.A: Portability for nurses to carry inside their uniform pockets
options.B: Zero electrical power consumption during operational hours
options.C: Support for thousands of concurrent users and massive data processing
options.D: Complete elimination of the need for cybersecurity protocols

explanation: Mainframes are designed to handle heavy multi-user workloads simultaneously without slowing down institutional databases. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary architectural feature that gives supercomputers their immense speed?

options.A: Manual data entry by clinical staff
options.C: Using analog sensors for continuous measurement

explanation: Supercomputers achieve incredible speed by dividing tasks across numerous processors working simultaneously in parallel. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which task is most appropriate for a supercomputer in a healthcare context?

options.A: Logging individual vital sign entries at a ward desk
options.B: Scanning barcodes on intravenous medication bags
options.C: Genomic sequencing and epidemiological disease modeling
options.D: Printing daily patient meal menus and duty rosters

explanation: Supercomputers handle massive computational loads like genetic research and public health modeling that ordinary computers cannot process quickly. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is a negative consequence of selecting inappropriate computer hardware for a clinical setting?

options.A: Workflow bottlenecks and compromised documentation safety
options.B: Instantaneous upgrading of all legacy software systems
options.C: Automatic reduction in hospital electricity utility bills
options.D: Immediate discovery of a cure for infectious diseases

explanation: Poor hardware choices disrupt clinical workflows and can negatively impact the accuracy and timeliness of patient records. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h7)

question: When nurse administrators evaluate new hospital technology, what factors must they balance?

options.A: Personal social media preferences of the nursing staff
options.B: Manufacturer stock market prices and global shipping routes
options.C: Processing needs, budget constraints, and clinical workflows
options.D: Keyboard aesthetic designs and office wall paint colors

explanation: Successful technology adoption depends on matching technical capabilities and financial costs with the practical needs of clinical staff. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h7)
